tools.name: audit_work
tools.description: Audits a piece of marketing (copy, landing page, email, ad, funnel or paywall, as text or a public URL) against Every Signal's teardowns of real companies and measured conversion rates. Returns a verdict, a 0-100 score, findings with the knowledge-base record ids behind them, concrete fixes and a re

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Returns the status and, when finished, the result of a job started by this account. Free.

tools.name: credits_balance
tools.description: Returns this account's Every Signal credit balance and the price of each tool. Free.

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description: Lists published Every Signal teardowns (title, short answer, key facts with evidence tags, link), optionally filtered by words. Free.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Returns one teardown by slug: the full text when the account has library access or bought the report, otherwise the public summary and key facts. Free.

tools.name: analyze_landing_page
tools.description: Analyzes one public page: tech stack and pixels, copy, speed and funnel signals, compared with how real companies in its sector sell. Returns ranked fixes and a hero rewrite. Uses 100 credits ($10). Runs 3-6 minutes and returns a job id.

tools.name: growth_audit
tools.description: Audits a domain's search footprint (ranked keywords, organic traffic estimate), tracking and growth signals against the growth moves and search patterns of real companies in its sector. Returns a ranked growth plan. Uses 150 credits ($15). Runs 3-6 minutes and returns a job id.

tools.name: intel_report
tools.description: Builds an automated snapshot of a company: tracking stack, top live Meta ads, search footprint and homepage, with a summary against its sector. Uses 490 credits ($49). Runs 6-12 minutes and returns a job id.

tools.name: analyze_ads
tools.description: Scores up to 10 ad creatives (public image URLs and/or ad text), or a brand's live Meta ads, against real companies' ad patterns. Returns fixes per creative and new hooks. Uses 150 credits ($15). Runs 1-6 minutes and returns a job id.

tools.name: kb_sectors
tools.description: Lists the sectors in the Every Signal knowledge base with record counts. Free (rate limited).

tools.name: kb_brief
tools.description: Returns a sector brief (markdown): hooks, offers, price points, funnel shapes and email patterns seen across the sector's records, with example record ids. Free (rate limited).

tools.name: kb_playbook
tools.description: Returns a task playbook (markdown) for homepage, email-campaign, paid-social-ads, subscription-funnel, checkout or geo work, built from the knowledge base. Free (rate limited).

tools.name: kb_search
tools.description: Full-text search across teardown records (homepage copy, ad copy, email copy, funnels, pricing, learnings). Returns matching record summaries. Costs 1 credit ($0.10) per call.

tools.name: kb_get
tools.description: Returns one knowledge-base record by id, optionally one section. Costs 1 credit ($0.10) per call.

tools.name: kb_examples
tools.description: Returns real examples of one section (for example ads or subscription_funnel) across a sector's records. Costs 1 credit ($0.10) per call.

tools.name: kb_benchmarks
tools.description: Returns measured conversion rates for one funnel across records (step-to-step rate, sample size, period, evidence tag); the median uses only 3 or more verified values. Costs 1 credit ($0.10) per call.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: kb_search · Private data: audit_work, kb_sectors, kb_brief, kb_search, kb_get, kb_examples, kb_benchmarks · Public sink: audit_work, kb_brief, kb_playbook, kb_search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: kb_search · Private data: audit_work, kb_sectors, kb_brief, kb_search, kb_get, kb_examples, kb_benchmarks · Public sink: audit_work, kb_brief, kb_playbook, kb_search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
